claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft", series "Defense Futures", published 2010-12-15 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2010-09-08, DIA document number DIA-08-1101-001. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.
Released PDF is 31 pages, marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO caveat partially illegible in the scan).
The DIA list transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee on 9 January 2018 reads 'Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ.'

The released cover page carries the date 15 December 2010, an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 8 September 2010 and document number DIA-08-1101-001 - the latest document number among the eight in this batch.

connections.edgeLabel: subject domain: cognitive load limits on multi-vehicle control
connections.label: Biology & Non-Human Biologics
connections.note: The commissioned question is how many unmanned vehicles a single human operator can control simultaneously - the human-factors constraint that would bound any swarming or multi-object control architecture. It forms a set with Genik's other two deliverables on limb-free control of external devices and on organic-molecule automation.
